what: a modelled thread on a hole that isn't the thread's size: refused with the size to use, never a silent change of the hole
method: Decision (#1018, #2853): a modelled thread never changes the size of the hole it is on; one that isn't the thread's size is refused, naming the size to use. A fill-to-tap-drill or turn-down option would be opt-in, off by default (see #3060), and get its own case. The refusal's numbers, from ISO 68-1 (H = P sqrt3/2, basic depth 5H/8): M5 (P 0.8): tap drill = 5 - 0.8 = 4.2 mm; basic depth 5H/8 = 5/8 x 0.8 x sqrt3/2 = 0.433 mm; a 5 mm hole is at the major diameter, so the internal thread (major d, minor d - 2 x 5H/8) cuts 0.00 mm. Expected message: "this 5 mm hole is too wide for a modelled M5 thread: it would cut 0.00 mm of the thread's 0.43 mm depth; drill 4.2 mm for M5, or thread this hole M6".
refusal: this 5 mm hole is too wide for a modelled M5 thread: it would cut 0.00 mm of the thread's 0.43 mm depth; drill 4.2 mm for M5, or thread this hole M6
